messages:
alex: Heads-up — our Go SDK is surfacing a generic `BadRequest` for a couple of parsing errors in the sampleapp onboarding flow. Users keep retrying and hitting 429s because clients treat it as retriable.

jess: ugh. do we know which endpoint?

alex: It seems to happen when the sampleapp sends malformed JSON for the `metadata` field to /v1/embeddings. The server returns 400 with body `{ "error": { "kind": "parse_error", "msg": "invalid metadata: expected object" } }`. SDK currently maps any 4xx -> BadRequest typed exception with no subtype.

maria: that explains the support tickets. we should expose a typed ParseError (non-retriable) vs ValidationError vs AuthError.

kai: agreed. For retries we rely on typed errors in client code. If all 4xx are bundled, libs like our sampleapp catch the wrong thing.

sam: can we do a quick patch in the Go/TS SDKs to inspect `error.kind` and set a specific error code? Minimal delta ideally.

alex: Proposed: map server side `error.kind` to typed exceptions. e.g. `parse_error` -> ParseError (non-retriable), `validation_error` -> ValidationError (non-retriable), `auth_error` -> AuthError (non-retriable), `rate_limited`/429 -> RateLimitError (retriable with backoff). Also include a `retry_hint` string from server when available.

jess: that sounds reasonable. sampleapp changes: stop blanket retry on any error and only retry on retriable typed errors.

maria: quick code sketch for Go SDK error type (pseudocode):

```go
// inside response unmarshal
switch payload.Error.Kind {
case "parse_error":
    return &errors.ParseError{Message: payload.Error.Msg, Retryable: false}
case "validation_error":
    return &errors.ValidationError{Message: payload.Error.Msg}
case "auth_error":
    return &errors.AuthError{Message: payload.Error.Msg}
default:
    return &errors.BadRequest{Message: payload.Error.Msg}
}
```

kai: add the `Retry-After` / `retry_hint` into RateLimitError so callers can backoff appropriately.

sam: operational question — do we need to change server contract to guarantee `error.kind`? Or are there other signals (headers) we can rely on?

alex: server already emits `error.kind` for many failures but it's not universal. Two action items: (1) server team to standardize `error.kind` on all 4xx responses, (2) SDKs to fallback to heuristics (header + message regex) if `error.kind` missing.

ci-bot: Note: created issue RN-447 (standardize error.kind) and linked to this thread.

jess: UX copy: make sure messages are concise. Instead of `BadRequest: invalid payload` we should show `Malformed metadata: expected JSON object` and show a hint 'See sampleapp metadata docs'.

alex: agreed. Also include a machine-readable `code` string in the top-level error for stable mapping (e.g., `ERR_PARSE_METADATA`).

maria: Devex/Docs task: update sampleapp onboarding README with a small FAQ on common parsing errors + how to interpret typed exceptions. I can draft.

kai: Also add a small test in the SDK test suite asserting mapping logic so we don't regress.

sam: timeline? can we cut a patch for Go & TS this week to stop the noisy retries?

jess: i'll take the TS SDK PR, alex will take the Go one. maria will file the docs PR. sam will follow up with infra to standardize error.kind.

alex: perfect. I'll add a changelog note: "SDK: add ParseError/ValidationError/RateLimitError -> better retry semantics for sample apps".

maria: thanks all. small QoL win for onboarding. :tada:

sam: ping me if CI flakiness pops up after the change, might be related to mock servers returning legacy shapes.

alex: noted — will run the sampleapp e2e and drop results here.
